title: Part 4 Practice: Human to Machine Interaction (HMI / HCI)

questions.text: What does the acronym HMI stand for in the context of this module?
options: A) Human-Machine Integration
B) Human-Machine Interaction
C) High-Memory Interface
D) Hardware-Management Interface
questions.explanation: The module starts section 1.4 with: 'Human-machine interaction (HMI) refers to the communication and interaction between a human and a machine via a user interface.'

questions.text: What are the three parts of Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) as defined in the module?
options: A) Hardware, Software, and Firmware
B) The user, the computer itself, and the ways they work together
C) Input, Output, and Processing
D) Data, Information, and Knowledge
questions.correct_answer: B) The user, the computer itself, and the ways they work together
questions.explanation: The module states: 'As its name implies, HCI consists of three parts: the user, the computer itself, and the ways they work together.'

questions.text: How do users typically interact with computers according to the module?
options: A) Through telepathy or mind control
B) Directly with hardware for input/output (like displays) and through a software interface (like a GUI)
C) By physically touching the motherboard
D) Through manual wiring and soldering
questions.correct_answer: B) Directly with hardware for input/output (like displays) and through a software interface (like a GUI)
questions.explanation: The module says: 'The user interacts directly with hardware for the human input and output such as displays, e.g. through a graphical user interface. The user interacts with the computer over this software interface using the given input and output (I/O) hardware.'

questions.text: What is the primary goal of Human-Computer Interaction (HCI)?
options: A) To eliminate the need for computers in daily life
B) To make computers more user-friendly and receptive to the user's needs
C) To increase the complexity of computer systems
D) To reduce the processing speed of computers
questions.correct_answer: B) To make computers more user-friendly and receptive to the user's needs
questions.explanation: The module states: 'The goal of HCI is to improve the interaction between users and computers by making computers more user-friendly and receptive to the user's needs.'

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT listed as a discipline contributing to HCI in the module?
options: A) Cognitive Psychology
B) Computer Science
C) Linguistics
D) Geology
questions.explanation: The module lists Cognitive Psychology, Computer Science, Linguistics, Engineering and Design, Artificial Intelligence, and Human Factors. Geology is not listed.

questions.text: What is a key advantage of good HCI design mentioned in the module?
options: A) It increases the cost of deployment
B) It reduces solution design time and integration complexity
C) It makes the system harder to use
D) It requires more extensive employee training
questions.correct_answer: B) It reduces solution design time and integration complexity
questions.explanation: The module states: 'They also reduce solution design time and integration complexity.' Other advantages include simplicity, ease of deployment, and cost savings.

questions.text: How does Cognitive Psychology contribute to HCI?
options: A) By building the actual software code
B) By studying human limitations, information processing, and learning
C) By designing the physical hardware
D) By analyzing network traffic
questions.correct_answer: B) By studying human limitations, information processing, and learning
questions.explanation: The module explains that Cognitive Psychology contributes to HCI by studying 'limitations, information processing, performance prediction, cooperative working, and capabilities.'

questions.text: Which discipline helps in designing voice user interfaces that understand natural languages like Amharic or Oromo?
options: A) Computer Science
B) Linguistics
C) Human Factors
D) Artificial Intelligence
questions.explanation: The module lists Linguistics as a contributing discipline. Linguistics helps in the design of natural language processing (NLP) and language-based interactions, ensuring the computer understands human language.

questions.text: What does the module state about 'natural user interfaces' like gestures?
options: A) They are outdated and rarely used today
B) They have gained increasing attention as they allow humans to control machines through natural and intuitive behaviors
C) They are only used in video games
D) They require extensive coding knowledge to use
questions.correct_answer: B) They have gained increasing attention as they allow humans to control machines through natural and intuitive behaviors
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Nowadays, natural user interfaces such as gestures have gained increasing attention as they allow humans to control machines through natural and intuitive behaviors.'

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the main advantages of HCI listed in the module?
options: A) Simplicity
B) Ease of deployment and operations
C) Cost savings for smaller set-ups
D) Increased integration complexity
questions.explanation: The module explicitly lists 'simplicity, ease of deployment & operations and cost savings for smaller set-ups' as advantages. It also states they 'reduce solution design time and integration complexity,' so increased complexity is the opposite of what HCI achieves.
